# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The two directions your survey leaves open cost the same number. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**The observation.** For two distinct **primes** p, q, the minimal base-field degree for a rank-2 object carrying both exponents (C127: φ(pq)/2) equals the genus of the Darmon–Granville pair-curve u^p + v^q = 1, which is (p−1)(q−1)/2. They are the same integer.

| signature | field degrees | pair-curve genera |
|---|---|---|
| (3,5,7) | 4, 12, 6 | 4, 12, 6 |
| (5,7,11) | 12, 30, 20 | 12, 30, 20 |
| (7,11,13) | 30, 60, 36 | 30, 60, 36 |

So the modular cost and the geometric cost of a pair of exponents coincide, and the survey's two live directions — a unifying modular object, and effective Diophantine geometry — meet the same barrier at the same size. For (3,5,7), Chabauty would need Jacobian rank below 4, 12 and 6 on the three pair-curves.

**Scope, found by the same computation and stated rather than glossed.** The identity holds *only* when both exponents are prime, because φ is multiplicative with φ(p) = p−1 but φ(4) = 2 while 4−1 = 3. It fails for (4,5) — degree 4, genus 6 — and for every pair with a composite exponent: 232 mismatches among coprime pairs below 25. It is a statement about prime signatures, which is where the open core lives, not a general identity.

Recorded as C137.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I narrowed the one named gap in the open-core statement, without closing it. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**The gap** was `cohen344`, the (3,4,4) input, unauditable because Cohen's *Number Theory II* is not available at zero budget. So I attacked it directly instead.

**Descent.** A³ = C⁴ − B⁴ = (C−B)(C+B)(C²+B²). With gcd(B,C) = 1 and B, C of opposite parity the three factors are pairwise coprime, so each is a cube: C−B = r³, C+B = s³, C²+B² = t³ with rst = A. Then 2C = r³+s³ and 2B = s³−r³, and substituting gives

> **r⁶ + s⁶ = 2t³** — signature (6,6,3) with coefficient 2.

The identity ((r³+s³)² + (s³−r³)²)/4 = (r⁶+s⁶)/2 was verified symbolically.

**Bounded search.** C < 400, every 1 ≤ B < C: no solution with the coprimality condition. The routine is calibrated — it recovers 1³+2³=3² on the (3,3,2) shape.

**Why the gap is narrowed, not closed.** The reduction covers only the opposite-parity branch; the same-parity case, where the factors share a 2, is untreated. And r⁶+s⁶ = 2t³ has **coefficient 2**, which no row I hold covers — BCDY Table 1's (3j,3k,n) is for coefficient 1.

So a future attempt now knows exactly which equation to attack. Recorded as C143.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The degree-12 form does not split over ℚ, and I identified the field where it does. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**Structure of W.** Substituting X = a²/b² turns W into the sextic

> p(X) = X⁶ + 114X⁵ − 705X⁴ + 1436X³ − 705X² + 114X + 1

which is **irreducible over ℚ**, with discriminant 2⁶²·3¹¹. It is palindromic, so Z = X + 1/X reduces it to the cubic **Z³ + 114Z² − 708Z + 1208**, whose real root is exactly

> −38 − 28·3^{1/3} − 20·3^{2/3}

verified by direct substitution (the expression simplifies to 0). Its discriminant is −2²²·3⁵, so the splitting field is ℚ(3^{1/3}, ω) and the natural field for W is the **pure cubic field ℚ(3^{1/3})**.

**Why that matters.** The appearance of 3^{1/3} is not an algebraic accident — the original equation is A³ + B⁴ = C⁴ and the descent passed through cubes at every step. The practical consequence is that this branch **cannot** be reduced to several small Thue equations over ℚ. It has to be attacked over a cubic field, which needs class-group and unit data for ℚ(3^{1/3}) — PARI-feasible in principle, not attempted here.

That is a concrete, named next step rather than an open-ended one. Recorded as C146 BLOCKED.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The branch from C144 is now attackable by a **complete** method, and every case computed is clean. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**The finding.** PARI's `thueinit`/`thue` succeeds on the sextic F(u,v) for which W(a,b) = F(a²,b²). Since `thue` is complete for each fixed right-hand side, running it over all cubes w³ for w = 1…60 enumerates **every** solution of F(u,v) = w³ in that range: 32 solutions in total, and **zero** with u and v both nonzero coprime squares — which is what the branch requires.

Non-empty right-hand sides were w = 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49. Most give only solutions with a zero coordinate; w = 16 gives eight, including (±3,±1) and (±1,±3), none with both coordinates squares.

**Field data, computed the same cycle.** ℚ(3^{1/3}) has discriminant −243, **class number 1**, unit rank 1 with fundamental unit x²−2. The cubic resolvent Z³+114Z²−708Z+1208 is *isomorphic* to it (`nfisisom` returns 1). The sextic has discriminant 11337408, signature [2,2], Galois group D(6) = S₃[×]2 of order 12.

**Honest limits.** The run is bounded at w ≤ 60 and proves nothing beyond it. Closing the branch needs either a bound on w — which would have to come from the size of the original solution — or a Thue–Mahler treatment with the right-hand side ranging over all cubes. The other two branches (3 dividing the gcd, and the same-parity case) are untouched.

Still, class number 1 and unit rank 1 make this tractable case by case — materially better than C145, where the congruence attack failed at every modulus. Recorded as C147.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

For the first time this session an open branch turns out to be **effectively** finite, not merely finite. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**The structure.** Dehomogenising F(u,v) = w³ at v = 1 gives the superelliptic curve

> w³ = p(u) = u⁶ + 114u⁵ − 705u⁴ + 1436u³ − 705u² + 114u + 1

with p squarefree (disc 2⁶²·3¹¹) of degree 6, so the curve has genus 4. Integral points on y³ = f(x) with f squarefree of degree ≥ 3 are finite and **effectively bounded** by Baker-type results (LeVeque). So this branch is a finite effective computation in principle, not an open-ended search.

**The computation.** Over |u| ≤ 20000 there are exactly **two** integral points: (0,1) and (3,16), with p(3) = 4096 = 16³ verified exactly. Neither is admissible — the branch requires u = a², and 3 is not a square.

**Why the difference in kind matters.** Darmon–Granville gives *ineffective* finiteness for a Beal signature. Here, after the descent, the surviving condition is a superelliptic equation for which effective bounds exist. That said, it is confined to one branch of the (3,4,4) input, and three gaps are named: the scan covers only b = ±1 and |u| ≤ 20000; the general homogeneous F(u,v) = w³ is Thue–Mahler and untouched; and the two other branches (3 dividing the gcd, and B, C both odd) remain open.

Recorded as C148.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The descent obstruction that usually kills this approach is absent. There is still no proof and no counterexample.

**The data.** For the sextic field K = ℚ[x]/(p), PARI's `bnfinit` gives:

- field discriminant 11337408 = 2⁶·3¹¹
- **class number 1**, trivial class group
- signature [2,2], unit rank 3, regulator 38.994…, torsion of order 2

**Why it matters.** In the standard descent for F(u,v) = w³, the ideal (u − θv) must be a cube times an ideal supported on the discriminant. Since **3 does not divide the class number**, that step is clean: the ideal is a cube outright, and u − θv = (unit)·γ³ with the unit ranging over a finite set of coset representatives mod cubes. Both relevant fields now have class number 1 — the pure cubic ℚ(3^{1/3}) from C147 and this sextic.

**What remains.** With unit rank 3 and torsion 2, there are at most 27 unit classes modulo cubes up to torsion, so the equation splits into a few dozen Thue-type equations over K — each still to be solved. That enumeration was **not** run: it needs explicit cube-coset representatives and a Thue solver over a sextic field, beyond what PARI does directly. The two other branches (3 dividing the gcd; B, C both odd) are untouched.

So this branch now stands as: effectively finite in theory, class number 1 with a clean cube step, no solution in any computed range. That is the most favourable position anything has reached this session — and it is still one branch of one input to the open-core statement. Recorded as C149.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

A named open obligation closed unconditionally, using only Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent 3. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The result.** For A³ + B⁴ = C⁴ with gcd(B,C) = 1 and B, C **both odd**, no solution exists. The argument:

1. C²+B² ≡ 2 mod 8, so v₂(C²+B²) = 1.
2. Exactly one of C−B, C+B has v₂ = 1 and the other has v₂ = k ≥ 2 — if both were 1, C would be even.
3. v₂(A³) = k+2 must be divisible by 3, so k ≡ 1 mod 3 and k ≥ 4. Hence 3 ∣ k−1 and **4^(k−1) is a perfect cube**.
4. The three odd parts are pairwise coprime, so each is a cube: C−B = 2^α μ³, C+B = 2^β ν³, (C²+B²)/2 = τ³.
5. With α = 1: C = μ³ + 2^(k−1)ν³, B = 2^(k−1)ν³ − μ³, giving (C²+B²)/2 = μ⁶ + 4^(k−1)ν⁶ = τ³.
6. Writing λ = 2^(2(k−1)/3): **(μ²)³ + (λν²)³ = τ³** — Fermat for exponent 3 in positive integers, impossible. The case α = k is symmetric.

**Checks.** Steps 1–2 verified over all odd coprime 1 ≤ B < C < 200 with zero violations; step 5's identity verified symbolically; direct control finds no solution of A³ = C⁴−B⁴ with odd coprime B < C < 600.

**Status: VERIFICATION_REQUIRED**, not PARTIAL_RESULT — it is not yet formalised in Lean nor independently re-derived. And it closes only one of the two parity branches; the opposite-parity branch, reducing to the degree-12 form, is untouched. Recorded as C151.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The surviving (3,4,4) branch now sits on a single named elliptic curve. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The finding.** The sextic p is palindromic — p(u) = u⁶p(1/u) — so the genus-4 curve w³ = p(u) carries the involution u ↦ 1/u, w ↦ w/u². Setting z = u + 1/u and W = w/u gives

> W³ = z³ + 114z² − 708z + 1208

a plane cubic, hence **genus 1**. PARI identifies it as the Mordell curve **y² = x³ − 972**: conductor 972, j-invariant 0, trivial torsion, **rank 1** by both the analytic rank and a 2-descent, generator P = (13, 35). Its integral points up to height 10⁷ are exactly (13, ±35); the multiples 2P through 14P are all non-integral with rapidly growing height.

**Why this does not close the branch.** The rank is 1, not 0, so the quotient has infinitely many rational points. Two further limits: z = u + 1/u sends integral u to a non-integral z unless u = ±1, so integral points do not correspond; and the points actually needed satisfy z = (u²+v²)/(uv) with u = a², v = b². Finishing would need elliptic Chabauty or a covering-collection argument over the relevant field — beyond the tooling available at zero budget.

Still, the obligation has gone from an abstract genus-4 object to a well-studied curve of conductor 972, and the method that would finish it is now named. Recorded as C153.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I cross-checked the quotient construction by an independent route and the two computations agree. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The check.** C153 identified the elliptic quotient using PARI. This cycle re-derived it in exact rational arithmetic, independently:

- The cubic W³ = z³+114z²−708z+1208 genuinely has a rational point — the point at infinity [1:1:0], since the leading coefficients of W³ and z³ are both 1 — so it is an elliptic curve, not a torsor.
- A direct search found the affine rational point **(z, W) = (10/3, 16/3)**, verified exactly: q(10/3) = 4096/27 = (16/3)³.
- Tracing it back: z = u + 1/u gives u = (z ± √(z²−4))/2, and z²−4 = 64/9 is a rational square, so **u = 3**.

**Why that matters.** C148 had found the integral point (u,w) = (3,16) on the genus-4 curve by a direct scan; C153 found the quotient by PARI. They are the *same point* — u = 3 gives z = 10/3 and W = w/u = 16/3. Two routes, one answer, so the quotient map is correct.

And u = 3 remains inadmissible: the branch needs u = a², and 3 is not a square — exactly why C148 rejected it. Recorded as C154.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I tried to use the square condition to cut down the rank-1 curve; it does not simplify. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**What was tried.** The branch needs u = a², v = b², so z = g + 1/g with g = (a/b)² a square. Writing g = h² gives z = h² + 1/h² = y² − 2. Substituting into W³ = q(z) yields

> W³ = Y³ + 108Y² − 1152Y + 3072,  Y = y²

**What happened.** That cubic is just q(Y−2) — a *shift* of the original, not a descent. PARI returns the same curve: minimal model y² = x³ − 972, conductor 972, j-invariant 0, trivial torsion, rank 1, generator (13,35). Nothing gained.

**What this pins down.** The square condition is the entire remaining content, and imposing it pulls back to a genus-4 cover again. So the obligation is now as sharp as it gets without new tooling:

> Find the rational points on y² = x³ − 972 (rank 1, generator (13,35)) whose corresponding Y-coordinate is a perfect square.

That is precisely **elliptic Chabauty over a quadratic field** — Bruin's method, the same tool Poonen–Schaefer–Stoll and Siksek–Stoll used for (2,3,7) and (3,4,5), the neighbouring signatures. It is not available at zero budget here.

A clean negative: the cheap route around the square condition does not exist, and the method that would finish is named. Recorded as C155 BLOCKED.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I tried to explain the (2,3)/(n,n) restriction structurally and the explanation failed. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The attempt.** Give A weight 1/x and B weight 1/y, so A^x + B^y is weighted-homogeneous of degree 1. Then 4P³ + 27Q² = c(A^x+B^y)^m forces P to have weighted degree m/3 and Q degree m/2, and a monomial A^i B^j has weighted degree i/x + j/y. That is a clean lattice condition, and I hoped it would single out (2,3) and (n,n).

**It does not.** Every pair (x,y) with 2 ≤ x,y ≤ 8 — all 49 — admits a weighted-homogeneous separating monomial pair for some m ≤ 12, including (3,5), (5,7), (7,8) and the rest of the open core. The 28 pairs outside the known families all pass the test.

**Why it fails.** The weighted-degree condition is necessary but nowhere near sufficient. It is bookkeeping on exponents and says nothing about whether the polynomial identity can actually hold. So the restriction found in C136 is genuinely **algebraic**, not numerological.

Recorded as C158 REFUTED, with the lemma that any explanation must use the identity itself — so this is not re-derived later as an apparent insight.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

A complete method now reaches the (3,4,4) survivor, and it finds the same inadmissible point for a third time. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The reformulation.** Writing Y = m/n in lowest terms, the branch condition becomes: the **cubic** binary form

> R(m,n) = m³ + 108m²n − 1152mn² + 3072n³

is a perfect cube, with m and n both squares (since Y = y²). R is irreducible over ℚ with discriminant −2²²·3⁵. PARI's `thue` is complete for each fixed right-hand side, so running it over all cubes w³ for w ≤ 80 enumerates **every** solution: 85 in total, **zero** with m and n both positive coprime squares.

Of the 85, eighty-three are degenerate with n = 0. The only two with n ≠ 0 are (16,3) at w = 16 — verified, R(16,3) = 4096 = 16³ — and (80,15), which is 5·(16,3) and not primitive. Y = 16/3 is not a square, so it is inadmissible.

**Third independent route to the same point.** C148 found (u,w) = (3,16) by a direct integral scan of the genus-4 curve; C154 found (z,W) = (10/3, 16/3) by a rational search on the elliptic quotient and traced it back to u = 3; C161 now finds (m,n) = (16,3) by complete Thue enumeration. Same point, three methods, inadmissible each time for the same reason.

This also supplies the positive control C156 was recorded as lacking. The run is bounded at w ≤ 80 and proves nothing beyond it; closing the branch still needs elliptic Chabauty. Recorded as C161.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I asked why three different methods kept returning the same point, and the answer is structural. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The explanation.** The recurring point (Y,W) = (16/3, 16/3) on the branch cubic W³ = Y³+108Y²−1152Y+3072 is where the line **W = Y is tangent** to the cubic. Substituting W = Y + s gives

> (3s−108)Y² + (3s²+1152)Y + (s³−3072) = 0

and at s = 0 this factors as **−12(3Y−16)²** — a double root at Y = 16/3. That line passes through the point at infinity [1:1:0], which is the rational point making the cubic an elliptic curve rather than a torsor.

So the point is the tangency of the distinguished line through the origin. C148 (integral scan of the genus-4 curve), C154 (rational search on the elliptic quotient) and C161 (complete Thue enumeration) were all bound to find it. It is inadmissible every time for the same reason: Y = 16/3 requires 3 to be a square.

**Useful by-product.** The parametrisation gives rational points on the branch cubic as rational s with

> −3s(s³ − 144s² − 2304s − 12288)

a square — a concrete quartic model of the same elliptic curve, in case a later attempt wants that form.

This retires a small mystery rather than advancing the conjecture. Recorded as C162.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# A flaw was found, so the claimed solution is not verified.

The flaw was in my own computation this cycle, caught and fixed before it was recorded as a result. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**What I built.** The parametrisation of the (3,4,4) survivor is now explicit. The quartic y² = D(s) has a rational root at s = 0, so s = 1/t gives the cubic w² = 36864t³ + 6912t² + 432t − 3, which is again y² = x³ − 972 — rank 1, **trivial torsion**, generator P = (1024, 143360) on that model. Trivial torsion and rank 1 mean **every** rational point is nP, so the branch is enumerable rather than merely searchable.

For n = 1…40: compute t = X(nP)/36864, then s = 1/t, then the roots Y of the quadratic, and test whether either is a positive rational square. **Zero admissible hits.**

**The flaw.** My first version used `sqrt()` and reported several admissible hits. PARI returns a floating-point root there, and `issquare` then tests a real number — so the hits were spurious. Redone with `issquare(D,&r)`, which is exact on rationals, the count drops to zero. This is precisely what the standing rule against floating point exists to prevent, and it produced a **false positive** — the dangerous direction. Recorded in C164 rather than quietly fixed.

**Still bounded.** n ≤ 40, and the n = 40 point already has hundreds of digits. Closing the branch needs a bound on n, which is what elliptic Chabauty supplies and what I still do not have.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The method C155 named as the finisher has a rank hypothesis, and I checked whether it can even be satisfied here. It can. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The condition.** Bruin's elliptic Chabauty over K needs rank_E(K) < [K:ℚ]. For K = ℚ(√d), rank_E(K) = rank_E(ℚ) + rank of the quadratic twist. Since rank_E(ℚ) = 1, the condition rank_E(K) < 2 holds **exactly when the twist y² = x³ − 972d³ has rank 0**.

**The result.** Computing twist ranks for all squarefree |d| ≤ 30, reporting only those where the lower and upper 2-descent bounds agree — so each rank is proved, not bounded:

- **twist rank 0** (condition met): d = −30, −23, −22, −15, −13, −11, −10, −1, 3, 5, 10
- twist rank 1: d = −29, −26, −19, −17, −14, −7, −6, −5, −3, −2, 2, 6, 11
- twist rank 2: d = −21, 7

Eleven usable fields in this small range.

**What this changes, and what it does not.** The obstruction to finishing the (3,4,4) survivor is now demonstrably **tooling, not arithmetic** — a system with `EllipticCurveChabauty` would have a genuine chance where PARI alone does not. But satisfying the rank condition is necessary, not sufficient: the actual computation needs the covering maps over K, the Mordell–Weil group over K with saturation, and the p-adic integration, none of which PARI provides. And d is not free — it must be the field over which the relevant covering splits, which I have not determined.

Recorded as C165.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# A flaw was found, so the claimed solution is not verified.

Second false positive in three cycles, again from my own termination logic rather than the mathematics. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**What I built.** A Mordell–Weil sieve on the (3,4,4) survivor — implementable in PARI because, unlike elliptic Chabauty, it needs no p-adic integration. Since E has rank 1 and trivial torsion, every rational point is nP; for each good prime p I reduce each residue class n mod ord(P), follow the map to Y, and exclude classes where Y cannot be a square mod p.

**The conditions from small primes are strong:** p = 5 and 7 force n even; p = 11 forces 4 ∣ n; p = 13 and 19 force 3 ∣ n; p = 29 forces 5 ∣ n — so n ≡ 0 mod 120 already.

**The flaw.** My first run stopped when one class survived and printed *"ONLY n = 0 SURVIVES at modulus 2"*. But a single surviving class 0 mod 2 means n is **even**, not n = 0. Removing the faulty break shows the true picture: the modulus grows to 391,514,760 with 280,665 surviving classes.

**And the honest limit.** A Mordell–Weil sieve cannot close this alone. It proves n ≡ 0 modulo a large N; ruling out n = N, 2N, … needs a **height bound**, which is exactly what elliptic Chabauty or a Baker-type bound supplies and what I still lack.

Both recent false positives came from a premature success condition — the `sqrt()` issue in C164 and this one. Recorded as C166.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The sieve's divisibility condition converts into a concrete size bound. There is still no proof of Beal and no counterexample.

**The result.** The Mordell–Weil sieve forces **120 ∣ n** using only the tiny primes 5, 7, 11, 13, 19, 29. Canonical heights grow as h(nP) = n²·h(P), and PARI gives h(P) = 2.9993679731… for the generator P = (1024, 143360). So any admissible point has canonical height at least 120²·h(P) = 43,190.9, and the numerator of its x-coordinate has roughly **37,500 decimal digits**.

Calibrated against the exactly computed multiples: numerator(x(nP)) has 4, 7, 15, 21, 35, 49, 66, 84 digits for n = 1…8, tracking n²·h(P) = 3.0, 12.0, 27.0, 48.0, 75.0, 108.0, 147.0, 192.0.

**Why it matters and what it is not.** It explains, rather than excuses, why every bounded search in C148, C156, C161 and C164 found nothing — any counterexample in this branch is astronomically large, so those nulls were never evidence and I am not treating them as such. But it is a **lower** bound, not an upper one, so it closes nothing. It applies only to the opposite-parity, d = 1 branch of (3,4,4), and the digit estimate uses the standard naive-versus-canonical height comparison rather than an explicit difference bound, so it is indicative rather than certified.

Also confirmed this cycle: PARI 2.17.4 has no integral-points routine, so the tooling gap identified in C165 is real.

| (iv) the three odd parts are pairwise coprime, hence cubes | prose |
| closing step: (μ²)³ + (λν²)³ = τ³ impossible by FLT3 | machine-checked |

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

Step (iii) has been upgraded from a hypothesis to a derived fact, and half the assembly is now machine-checked; the remaining prose is the factorisation-and-substitution glue for one restricted case that, by C157, cannot reach Beal's open core anyway. No proof, no counterexample.

**Two new theorems**, `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, full `lake build` clean:

- `two_pow_mul_odd_inj` — the decomposition `n = 2^e · odd` is unique in *both* components. Induction on `e`, cancelling a factor 2 at each step.
- `odd_part_cube` — if `2^e · P = A³` with `P` odd, then `3 ∣ e` **and** `P` is a cube.

The second one matters beyond bookkeeping: step (iii) previously *assumed* `3 ∣ k+2` as a hypothesis of `k_mod_three_of_three_dvd`. `odd_part_cube` derives it, so that divisibility is no longer an input to the descent.

**What is left in the branch** is a single glue lemma: derive `A³ = (C−B)(C+B)(C²+B²)` from the branch hypotheses, apply `odd_part_cube` to its 2-part, feed the odd parts through `isCoprime_of_forall_common_unit` → `three_coprime_factors_cubes`, and substitute into `no_sixth_power_cube_relation`. Every piece it consumes now exists; the header table marks it as the one prose row.

I'll say plainly what this is worth: (3,4,4) has two equal exponents, so the factorisation `C⁴−B⁴` exists. The open core of Beal has three pairwise distinct reduced exponents and no such factorisation, which is the same "two exponents, not three" boundary that the rigidity budget and the Frey-discriminant search independently produced. Finishing this branch closes a known-closed case more cleanly; it does not move that boundary.

# Katz rigidity and the exponent budget (U253–U256, pool C120/C121)

Why no *rigid* local system can carry three independent Beal exponents.

For a local system of rank `n` on `P¹ ∖ {0,1,∞}` with semisimple local monodromies whose
eigenvalue multiplicities are the parts of three partitions of `n`, Katz's rigidity index is

    rig = -n² + (sum of squares of all the multiplicities),

and the system is **rigid** exactly when `rig = 2`.

Two facts are formalised here.

* `rigid_regular_semisimple_iff` — if all three local monodromies are *regular semisimple*
  (`n` distinct eigenvalues at each puncture, which is what monodromy of order `x` acting with
  distinct eigenvalues gives), then every multiplicity is `1`, the sum of squares is `3n`, and
  rigidity forces `n = 1` or `n = 2`.  Rank `2` is the classical hypergeometric `₂F₁` /
  elliptic-curve Frey situation, already exploited one signature at a time.

* `rigid_max_budget_attained` — the triple `((n-1,1), (1ⁿ), (1ⁿ))` is rigid for **every** `n`,
  by the identity `-n² + ((n-1)² + 1) + n + n = 2`.  Its total number of distinct eigenvalues is
  `2n+2`, one puncture being reduced to just two.

The matching upper bound (no rigid triple exceeds `2n+2` distinct eigenvalues) is verified
exhaustively for `2 ≤ n ≤ 14` in `code/U254_rigid_eigenvalue_budget.py`; it is recorded in the
pool as C121 and is *not* claimed here.

Since regular-semisimple monodromy at all three punctures needs `3n` distinct eigenvalues and
`2n+2 ≥ 3n` only at `n = 2`, the deficit `n-2` is the exact amount of exponent information that
rigidity costs.  This is a statement about the *obstruction*, not a step toward a proof of Beal.

No `sorry`, no custom `axiom`s; mathlib only.
-/

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# A flaw was found, so the claimed solution is not verified.

My own rigidity obstruction — the result I had recorded as the reason no object can carry three independent Beal exponents — is **refuted as stated**, by exact enumeration in [U309_rigidity_countersearch.py](code/U309_rigidity_countersearch.py). Rigidity does not forbid three independent exponents, which reopens the survey's "unifying motivic object" direction rather than closing it. Beal itself is untouched: no proof, no counterexample.

**The error.** U258 silently identified two different conditions:

- *local monodromy has **order** `x`* — what a Beal exponent actually forces;
- *local monodromy is **regular semisimple** with eigenvalues of order `x`* — what the rigidity-index computation assumes.

A pseudoreflection with partition `(n−1,1)` has order equal to the order of its single non-trivial eigenvalue, so it realises **any** order using only two distinct eigenvalues. The hypergeometric triple `((1ⁿ),(1ⁿ),(n−1,1))` therefore has `rig = 2` at every rank and carries three pairwise distinct orders: `(3,4,5)` at `n=3`, `(3,5,7)` at `n=5`, `(3,7,11)` at `n=6`.

**Both U258 computations were re-run as controls and both stand** — regular-semisimple-at-all-three is rigid only for `n = 1,2`, and the `2n+2` eigenvalue budget is attained by `((n−1,1),(1ⁿ),(1ⁿ))`. The arithmetic was never wrong; the reading of it was.

**Propagated to all four layers** per the layering rule that bit this repo before: the Lean header in [Rigidity.lean](formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean) (build still clean, theorems untouched — only the withdrawn headline), the [U258 checkpoint](research/checkpoints/U258_rigidity_obstruction.md), [VERIFIED.md](VERIFIED.md), and the memory item. New candidate C169 records it with its own obligations.

**What this is worth.** It removes a wrong reason for pessimism; it supplies no Frey object. Whether a Katz hypergeometric sheaf with those local orders can be attached to `Aˣ+Bʸ=C^z` over ℚ — with a Galois-stable eigenvalue set, the right one-parameter base, and a usable motivic realisation — is entirely open, and C169 records those three obligations as unaddressed.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

Rationality does not restore the obstruction I withdrew last cycle — rigid ℚ-rational triples with three pairwise distinct exponents exist, the smallest at rank 4 with orders (3,4,5) — but the exact minimal rank for a ℚ-rational monodromy of order `m` is `φ(m)`, which converts the obstruction from existence into **growth**. Beal is untouched: no proof, no counterexample.

**The test (C169 obligation c).** A local system over ℚ has local characteristic polynomials in ℚ[T], so each eigenvalue multiset is Galois-stable: one multiplicity `c_d` per divisor `d ∣ m`, applied to all `φ(d)` primitive `d`-th roots at once, with order exactly `m` iff `c_m ≥ 1`. That is a finite exact check, run in [U310_galois_stable_rigid.py](code/U310_galois_stable_rigid.py) over ranks 2–10.

I expected this to kill the U309 witness, because the pseudoreflection `(n−1,1)` is **not** rational for any `m ≥ 3` — a lone primitive `m`-th root of multiplicity 1 is not Galois-stable. It doesn't. Other partitions take over: **252 rigid ℚ-rational triples** with three pairwise distinct exponents, smallest rank 4, orders (3,4,5), partitions `((2,1,1),(2,2),(1⁴))`, `rig = −16+6+8+4 = 2`.

**What did come out is sharp.** Minimal rank for order `m` over ℚ, computed exactly:

| m | 3 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 11 | 13 | 17 | 19 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| min rank | 2 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 10 | 12 | 16 | 18 |

— exactly `φ(m)` every time. And minimal rank for a full rigid rational triple: (3,4,5)→4, (3,5,7)→9, (5,7,11)→20, (7,11,13)→none below rank 25.

Two theorems added to [Rigidity.lean](formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean), build clean: `rank_ge_totient` (the `φ(m)` lower bound) and `smallest_rational_rigid_witness` (the rank-4 counterwitness to my own withdrawn headline). Recorded as C170, with four obligations left explicitly untested — chiefly that the combinatorial model captures ℚ-rationality of the actual sheaf, and C169's untouched (a) attachment to `Aˣ+Bʸ=C^z` and (b) motivic realisation.

The honest summary of two cycles: I replaced a wrong obstruction with a correct one of a different kind. Existence at a fixed signature is not the problem; the rank growing like `φ` of the largest exponent is.

```
namespace Beal

/-- **The bases are pairwise coprime: `gcd A B = 1`.**
A prime dividing `A` and `B` divides `A^x + B^y = C^z`, hence divides `C`, hence divides
`gcd (gcd A B) C = 1`. -/
theorem gcd_ab_eq_one {A B C x y z : ℕ} (h : IsBealCounterexample A B C x y z) :
    Nat.gcd A B = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨hA, hB, hC, hx, hy, hz, hgcd, heq⟩ := h
  rw [Nat.eq_one_iff_not_exists_prime_dvd]
  rintro p hp hdvd
  have hpA : p ∣ A := hdvd.trans (Nat.gcd_dvd_left A B)
  have hpB : p ∣ B := hdvd.trans (Nat.gcd_dvd_right A B)
  have hpC : p ∣ C := by
    refine hp.dvd_of_dvd_pow (n := z) ?_
    rw [← heq]
    exact Nat.dvd_add (dvd_pow hpA (by omega)) (dvd_pow hpB (by omega))
  have hfin : p ∣ gcd3 A B C := by
    unfold gcd3
    exact Nat.dvd_gcd hpA (Nat.dvd_gcd hpB hpC)
  rw [hgcd] at hfin
  exact hp.one_lt.ne' (Nat.dvd_one.mp hfin)

/-- `gcd A C = 1`.  A prime dividing `A` and `C` divides `B^y = C^z - A^x`. -/
theorem gcd_ac_eq_one {A B C x y z : ℕ} (h : IsBealCounterexample A B C x y z) :
    Nat.gcd A C = 1 := by
  have hab := gcd_ab_eq_one h
  obtain ⟨hA, hB, hC, hx, hy, hz, hgcd, heq⟩ := h
  rw [Nat.eq_one_iff_not_exists_prime_dvd]
  rintro p hp hdvd
```

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The second of C169's three obligations also fails to obstruct: the Beal specialisation point is tame at every prime dividing `ABC`, unconditionally, for a coprime solution — now machine-checked. After three cycles of elimination the three-exponent local-system route has exactly one surviving obstruction, automorphy of rank-`n` motives, so I have marked it BLOCKED rather than open. No proof, no counterexample.

**The test (C169 obligation a).** A solution gives `t = A^x/C^z` with `1−t = B^y/C^z`. For a sheaf with local orders `(x,y,z)` to pull back unramified, each `p`-adic valuation must be divisible by the matching order. [U311_tame_specialisation.py](code/U311_tame_specialisation.py) checks this on exact integers: 56 valuations across the ten Fermat–Catalan solutions, all pass.

**The first run reported failures, and they were the interesting part.** `3³+6³=3⁵`, `7⁶+7⁷=98³` and `2⁹+8³=4⁵` all violated the condition at the prime dividing `C`. Not a bug — those have `gcd > 1`, and the condition is false without coprimality. They are now controls, and their failure is required; a version of this test that passed on them would be vacuous. This also settles the circularity worry: a Beal counterexample has `gcd = 1` by definition, so coprimality is the counterexample hypothesis, not a smuggled assumption.

**Four theorems added** to [Structure.lean](formal/Beal/Structure.lean), all `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, build clean: `support_disjoint_A`, `support_disjoint_C` (a prime divides at most one base), and `tame_valuation_at_A`, `tame_valuation_at_C` (the surviving valuation is a multiple of that base's own exponent). The `C` case is the one that is easy to state wrongly — the divisibility there is by `z`, not `x` or `y`.

**Where this leaves the route** (recorded as C171, status BLOCKED): rigidity permits three distinct orders, ℚ-rationality permits them at rank ≥ `φ(m)`, and the specialisation is tame. What is missing is automorphy of an `n`-dimensional motive over ℚ for `n > 2` — a named open problem, not something reachable at $0. The three cycles converted "no Frey object is known for three exponents" into one specific missing theorem. That is a sharper obstruction, not progress toward a proof.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The (3,4,4) same-parity assembly is now machine-checked down to a single substitution; [ThreeFourFour.lean](formal/Beal/ThreeFourFour.lean) holds 23 theorems with no `sorry` and no custom axioms. Beal's open core is unaffected by this, as recorded. No proof, no counterexample.

**Six theorems added**, all `[propext, Quot.sound]` or `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, build clean:

- `quartic_factorisation` — `A³ = (C−B)(C+B)(C²+B²)`. The ℕ-subtraction fought back; substituting `C = B+d` removes it entirely.
- `sq_sum_two_mul_odd`, `descent_two_adic` — splits all three factors as `2^e · odd` and returns **both** `3 ∣ a+b+1` and "the product of the odd parts is a cube", from `odd_part_cube`. The divisibility is derived, never assumed.
- `odd_parts_cubes` — the join: casts to ℤ, routes every odd common divisor through the three `odd_common_divisor_*` lemmas via `isCoprime_of_forall_common_unit`, lands in `three_coprime_factors_cubes`.
- `two_exponents` — `1 ≤ a`, `1 ≤ b`, and `a = 1 ∨ b = 1`; if both were `≥ 2` then `4 ∣ 2B` and `B` would be even.
- `nat_cube_of_int_cube` — a positive natural that is an integer cube is a natural cube.

**What is left is one step**, and the header names it precisely: from `C−B = 2^aμ³`, `C+B = 2^bν³`, `C²+B² = 2τ³` with `a = 1`, get `τ³ = μ⁶ + 4^(b−1)ν⁶`, then `four_pow_cube_of_valuation` and `no_sixth_power_cube_relation` close it; `b = 1` is symmetric. Every lemma that step consumes now exists in the file.

Restating the value honestly, since it hasn't changed: (3,4,4) has two equal exponents, which is what makes `C⁴−B⁴` factor. Beal's open core has three pairwise distinct reduced exponents and no such factorisation. Finishing this branch closes a case already closed in the literature, more cleanly and with the citation replaced by machine-checked mathlib; it does not advance the open core.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The (3,4,4) same-parity branch is now closed with **no prose step**: `three_four_four_same_parity` is machine-checked end to end, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, sole external input mathlib's `fermatLastTheoremThree`. This closes a case already closed in the literature and does not reach Beal's open core. No proof of the conjecture, no counterexample.

**The statement**, checked by `#check`:

```
∀ {A B C : ℕ}, 0 < A → Odd B → Odd C → B < C → Nat.Coprime B C → A^3 + B^4 = C^4 → False
```

**The last step.** `(C−B)² + (C+B)² = 2(C²+B²)` gives `4^a u² + 4^b v² = 4w`; `two_exponents` forces exactly one of `a,b` to be 1 (strengthened this cycle with `¬(a=1 ∧ b=1)` — if both were 1 then `C = u+v` is even); cancelling the 4 leaves `w = u² + 4^(b−1)v²`; the odd parts are cubes, `3 ∣ a+b+1` makes `4^(b−1)` a cube, and Fermat's exponent 3 closes it. The `b=1` case is the mirror image.

[ThreeFourFour.lean](formal/Beal/ThreeFourFour.lean) is now 25 theorems, no `sorry`, no custom axioms, full build clean. The 9,116-pair numerical check in `code/` is demoted from support to redundant evidence.

**What this is and isn't.** It replaces an unauditable Cohen citation — the one hypothesis of `final_residual` I could not check at $0 — with a machine-checked proof. That is an audit improvement. The descent needs `C⁴−B⁴` to factor, i.e. `gcd(y,z) > 1`, which among reduced exponents means two exponents are equal; Beal's open core has three pairwise distinct ones and no such factorisation. The opposite-parity branch of (3,4,4) still reduces to the Mordell curve `y² = x³−972` and needs elliptic Chabauty, which PARI cannot do and I cannot buy.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The opposite-parity branch of (3,4,4) does **not** need elliptic Chabauty — I had that wrong. All three factors are odd there, so the branch reduces directly to Euler's equation `a³+b³=2c³`, and that reduction is now machine-checked. Beal's open core is still untouched: no proof, no counterexample.

**The observation.** When exactly one of `B,C` is even, `C−B`, `C+B` and `C²+B²` are all odd. The 2-adic bookkeeping that made the same-parity branch difficult simply does not arise — the three factors are pairwise coprime and each is a cube outright. With `C−B = μ³`, `C+B = ν³`, the identity `(C−B)² + (C+B)² = 2(C²+B²)` gives

```
(μ²)³ + (ν²)³ = 2τ³
```

Euler's theorem says the only coprime solutions of `a³+b³=2c³` have `a=b`, forcing `μ=ν`, hence `B=0`, excluded.

**Machine-checked:** `opposite_parity_reduction`, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, plus `sq_mod_two` and `opposite_parity_factors_odd`. Numerical support in [U315_opposite_parity.py](code/U315_opposite_parity.py): 32,335 opposite-parity coprime pairs with all three factors odd and pairwise coprime, 364 reconstruction identities, and no `a³+b³=2c³` with `a≠b` below 3,000.

**What is formalised is the reduction, not the closure.** Euler's theorem is not in mathlib — I checked by grep; `Mathlib/NumberTheory/FLT/` has only `Basic`, `Four`, `MasonStothers`, `Three`. The bounded search above is not evidence for it, per the survey gate. So the branch now depends on a classical named theorem that is formalisable, instead of on a computation this project cannot run. That converts the obstruction from **tooling** to **work**.

The Mordell-curve analysis in the U278 checkpoint (rank 1, generator `(13,35)`, the `120 ∣ n` sieve) is correct and preserved — it is just unnecessary. C155/C156 are annotated as superseded rather than refuted, and C172 records the new route with its one open obligation.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

The last unauditable citation in `final_residual` is gone: `cohen344` is now derived from a single named 1770 theorem by a machine-checked argument, with the same-parity half needing no hypothesis at all. Euler's `a³+b³=2c³` is stated but not proved, and none of this reaches Beal's open core. No proof, no counterexample.

**New file** [Cohen344.lean](formal/Beal/Cohen344.lean), in the root build, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`:

```
cohen344_of_euler : EulerCubicTwo → NoCoprimeSol 3 4 4
```

The proof splits on the parity of `b` and `c` (they cannot both be even, being coprime): both odd is closed **outright** by `three_four_four_same_parity` with no hypothesis used; opposite parity goes through `opposite_parity_reduction`, where `a = b` forces `C−B = C+B`, hence `B = 0`.

**I checked whether mathlib's FLT3 machinery could discharge Euler and it cannot.** `FermatLastTheoremForThreeGen` covers `a³+b³ = u·c³` for a **unit** `u` in `𝓞 K`; our `u = 2` is not a unit in ℤ[ζ₃]. The classical route is a separate descent (`a = u+v`, `b = u−v` giving `u(u²+3v²) = c³`, then factorisation in ℤ[ω]) — a multi-hundred-line formalisation I did not attempt this cycle.

**What changed and what didn't.** `final_residual` previously rested on a book I do not hold, with no way to audit it at $0; it now rests on a named classical result with the gap explicit in the type signature. That is an audit improvement, not a new theorem about Beal. By C157 the entire (3,4,4) line needs `gcd(y,z) > 1` and cannot touch the open core of three pairwise distinct reduced exponents.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

My own C171 was too weak: the three-exponent object is **never regular**, so the regular-weight potential-automorphy theorems are structurally inapplicable to it, not merely unproved. That is a second obstruction of a different kind, and it does not bring a resolution any closer — no proof, no counterexample.

**The argument.** Every potential-automorphy theorem available in rank > 2 requires distinct Hodge–Tate weights, which for a local system on `P¹∖{0,1,∞}` means partition `(1ⁿ)` at both `0` and `∞`. Those contribute `n+n` to the rigidity budget, so `rig = 2` forces the third puncture to contribute `n²−2n+2` — the pseudoreflection `(n−1,1)`. And a pseudoreflection is ℚ-rational only when `φ(m) = 1`, i.e. `m ≤ 2`, which the Beal exponent range excludes.

[U317_regularity_obstruction.py](code/U317_regularity_obstruction.py): of **792** rigid ℚ-rational triples with three pairwise distinct reduced exponents at ranks 2–14, **zero** are regular at both punctures; `(n−1,1)` is ℚ-rational for **no** reduced exponent at ranks 3–8.

**Self-duality was checked and is free** — a Galois orbit over ℚ is closed under `α ↦ α⁻¹` because `−1` is coprime to `m`. Only regularity bites, which is why this is worth recording rather than assuming.

**Four theorems** in [Rigidity.lean](formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean), axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, build clean: `regular_forces_pseudoreflection`, `pseudoreflection_budget`, `rational_pseudoreflection_order_le_two`, `no_rational_pseudoreflection_for_exponent`.

C171 is corrected in place rather than withdrawn — everything else it recorded stands. C174 carries the new statement with its modelling assumptions listed explicitly (the step from "defined over ℚ" to the Galois-stable multiplicity model is standard but not formalised) and the untested escapes named: non-rigid families, larger base fields, irregular-weight automorphy of Calegari–Geraghty type, and objects that are not local systems.

The pattern across six cycles: each thing I expected to obstruct this route didn't, and the one that does is the one I'd assumed was merely a missing theorem.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I tested C174's first named escape and it **closes**: the regularity obstruction does not use rigidity at all, so dropping rigidity buys nothing. Over ℚ, regular weights and three pairwise distinct Beal exponents are incompatible for *any* local system on the thrice-punctured line. Still no proof, no counterexample.

**The mechanism is arithmetic, not geometric.** Regular semisimplicity at a puncture of order `m` means every multiplicity is 1, so over ℚ the eigenvalue multiset is a union of *whole* Galois orbits taken once:

```
n = Σ φ(d) over a set of divisors of m containing m    ⟹    φ(m) ≤ n ≤ Σ_{d|m} φ(d) = m
```

For three pairwise distinct reduced exponents `p < q < r`, the largest must be an odd prime (if `r = 4` there is only one smaller reduced exponent), so `φ(r) = r−1 > p ≥ n`. The intervals cannot meet. No rigidity index appears anywhere in that argument.

[U318_regularity_without_rigidity.py](code/U318_regularity_without_rigidity.py): all **165** pairwise-distinct triples from `{3,4,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31}` give an empty rank set. **Controls confirm it isn't vacuous** — `(p,p,p)` is non-empty for every `p`, and the mixed cases `(3,3,4) → {2,3}` and `(4,4,5) → {4}` are non-empty. That last one is a pleasing consistency check: rank 4 at `(4,4,5)` is the neighbourhood where Siksek–Stoll actually works.

**Three theorems** in [Rigidity.lean](formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean), axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, build clean: `regular_rank_upper` (via `Nat.sum_totient`), `regular_rank_lower`, `no_common_regular_rank`.

**What remains untested** in this line, recorded on C174/C175: base fields larger than ℚ — where Galois orbits shrink and the intervals widen, which is the one escape I'd now expect to be live — irregular-weight automorphy of Calegari–Geraghty type, and objects that are not local systems. The modelling step from "defined over ℚ" to the Galois-stable multiplicity model remains standard-but-unformalised, and I have kept that caveat attached to both candidates.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I tested the second escape and it is **real and cheap**, so I have corrected my own scope claim: the regularity obstruction of C174/C175 holds over ℚ only, not field-independently. It still yields no route, because over a larger field the method needs automorphy in rank > 2 over that field — harder, not easier. No proof, no counterexample.

**Two measures of the escape's cost**, both computed exactly in [U319_base_field_escape.py](code/U319_base_field_escape.py) over all 56 pairwise-distinct triples from `{3,4,5,7,11,13,17,19}`:

| reading | requirement | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `K` contains all three roots of unity | `[K:ℚ] ≥ φ(lcm(p,q,r)) = (p−1)(q−1)(r−1)` | 16 → 3456 |
| `K` only shrinks the largest orbit to the smallest ceiling | `[K:ℚ] ≥ φ(r)/p` | **2 → 6** |

The second is the binding one. Quoting only the first would have overstated the obstruction in precisely the way U258 was overstated before U309 caught it — so I have propagated the correction into the [Rigidity.lean](formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean) header and onto C174 and C175, rather than leaving the stronger-sounding version standing.

**Why the escape still doesn't help.** Over `K` the obstruction becomes C171 again: automorphy of an `n`-dimensional motive with `n > 2`, now over a number field. That is consistent with what the literature actually does — the (5,5,p) work uses ℚ(√5) at **rank 2** and stops there. Recorded as C176 with the untested parts named: whether a degree 2–6 field can carry a Frey object for three independent exponents with the right residual representation, and whether the resulting statement descends to ℚ at all, since the Beal solution itself lives over ℚ.

Two escapes tested, one closed and one open-but-unhelpful. The remaining named ones are irregular-weight automorphy of Calegari–Geraghty type and objects that are not local systems.

That makes the remaining work schedulable rather than open-ended; it still does not touch Beal's open core. No proof, no counterexample.

**New file** [Euler.lean](formal/Beal/Euler.lean), in the root build, all `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`:

- `euler_both_odd` — in `a³+b³ = 2c³` with `a,b` coprime, both are odd. From `n³ ≡ n (mod 2)` they share parity; both-even contradicts coprimality.
- `euler_identity` — `(p+q)³ + (p−q)³ = 2p(p²+3q²)`, one `ring` call.

- `cohen344_of_descent : EulerDescentStep → NoCoprimeSol 3 4 4`.

**The residual gap is now exactly one line:**

```
EulerDescentStep : IsCoprime p q → p * (p^2 + 3*q^2) = c^3 → q = 0
```

**Feasibility, checked rather than guessed.** That step factors `p²+3q²` in ℤ[ω], which needs unique factorisation there — and mathlib has it: `three_pid` in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PID.lean` gives `IsPrincipalIdealRing (𝓞 K)` for `K = ℚ(ζ₃)`. The unit group has order 6, so cube extraction needs unit bookkeeping rather than a `Subsingleton` instance — the same obstacle `Int.eq_pow_of_mul_eq_pow_odd` solved over ℤ. I estimate a few hundred lines and did not attempt it this cycle; C177 records that estimate and the confirmed prerequisite rather than leaving "needs a classical theorem" vague.

Scope is unchanged and I will keep saying so: (3,4,4) requires `gcd(y,z) > 1`, so even fully unconditional it cannot reach the open core of three pairwise distinct reduced exponents.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# A flaw was found, so the claimed solution is not verified.

The `EulerDescentStep` I recorded last cycle as "the residual gap" was **false as stated** — `p = 0, q = 1, c = 0` satisfies it with `q ≠ 0` — so a Prop that can never be proved was sitting at the bottom of the (3,4,4) chain. Fixed by adding `p ≠ 0`, which the reduction does supply; exact re-search finds no witness with `0 < p` up to 4000. Beal itself is unaffected: still no proof, no counterexample.

**The counterexample.** `IsCoprime 0 1` holds in ℤ (`0·0 + 1·1 = 1`) and `0·(0² + 3·1²) = 0 = 0³`, yet `q = 1 ≠ 0`.

**Why this was the dangerous direction.** `euler_of_descent` was not *wrong* — an implication from a false hypothesis is still a theorem, and `lake build` stayed green throughout. It was **vacuous**, and everything downstream (`cohen344_of_descent`) compiled exactly as if it were meaningful. Nothing in the type-checking would ever have caught it. I found it only because I ran a counterexample search against my own newly-recorded Prop before trying to prove it.

**The fix**, in [Euler.lean](formal/Beal/Euler.lean):

```
EulerDescentStep : p ≠ 0 → IsCoprime p q → p * (p^2 + 3*q^2) = c^3 → q = 0
```

`euler_of_descent` now proves `hppos : p ≠ 0` explicitly from `p = (a+b)/2` with `a,b > 0`. Build clean, axioms unchanged. Exact search: **no** witness with `0 < p, q ≠ 0` over `1 ≤ p,q ≤ 4000`, and none over `−1200 ≤ p < 0` either.

**Preserved, not overwritten.** C177 keeps the wrong version alongside the correction, and the counterexample is now a permanent assertion in [U320_regression_checks.py](code/U320_regression_checks.py) (7 checks, in the harness) so the hypothesis cannot be dropped again silently.

**Lesson recorded on C177:** state a `Prop`, then counterexample-search it *before* recording it as the residual gap. A vacuous hypothesis is worse than a wrong theorem, because the proof assistant endorses everything built on it.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I turned last cycle's flaw into a standing audit: all fourteen named hypothesis `Prop`s in the Lean development have now been counterexample-searched, and none is false for a degenerate reason. That closes the specific hole that made `EulerDescentStep` vacuous, but proves none of them and changes nothing about the open core. No proof, no counterexample.

**Why the whole hypothesis layer needed this.** A false named `Prop` makes `final_residual` vacuous while `lake build` stays green — Lean cannot notice, because an implication from a false hypothesis is still a theorem. That is the assumption boundary, and it is where this repo's layering defect is most dangerous.

[U323_named_prop_countersearch.py](code/U323_named_prop_countersearch.py) checks each one over an exact finite range:

`EulerCubicTwo` · `EulerDescentStep` (fixed form) · `FLTHyp` · `DarmonMerelNN2` · `DarmonMerelNN3` · `BCDYThreeThreeTwoN` · `BEN24n` · `BCDYFourTwoNThree` · `DahmenSiksek` · `InstanceRows` at (3,4,4), (3,4,7), (3,4,5) · `Quartic400g2` · `Quartic400b2` — all clean.

**The control is the part that makes it mean anything.** The script first runs its own searcher against the *known-false* version of `EulerDescentStep` and aborts unless it reports `(0,1,0)`. It does. So a clean line is a real negative rather than a blind searcher — the same non-vacuity discipline I applied to U317/U318.

Registered in the harness (now 69/69, which still means "69 scripts ran"), so a future edit that weakens a hypothesis into falsity fails rather than passing silently.

**What this explicitly is not:** a proof of any of the fourteen. They are statements of published theorems, and bounded search is a dead category by the survey gate. Two of them — `EulerCubicTwo` and `EulerDescentStep` — remain the live gap in the (3,4,4) chain; the other twelve are citations whose primary sources are not all held in `references/`. The open core, three pairwise distinct reduced exponents, is untouched by any of this.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I tested a shortcut that would have closed the opposite-parity (3,4,4) branch without Euler's theorem, and **refuted it** — the square-target variants have abundant solutions, so Euler's cube-target form is genuinely required. Nothing here touches the open core. No proof, no counterexample.

**The shortcut.** The descent gives three simultaneous conditions, not one. Since `τ³ = C²+B²` and `(μν)³ = C²−B²`:

```
τ³ + (μν)³ = 2C²        τ³ − (μν)³ = 2B²
```

If either `x³ ± y³ = 2z²` forced `x = y`, the branch would close with no Euler input at all.

**Neither does.** Exact search: `x³+y³ = 2z²` has at least 10 coprime solutions with `x ≠ y` below 3000 — smallest `(13,11,42)` and `(23,1,78)`; `x³−y³ = 2z²` has at least 18, smallest `(5,3,7)`. Verified exactly: `13³+11³ = 2·42²`, `23³+1³ = 2·78²`, `5³−3³ = 2·7²`.

**What that tells me:** the cube on the right-hand side of `a³+b³ = 2c³` is doing the work, not the factor 2 or the sum-of-cubes shape. Euler cannot be traded for a weaker cousin, which sharpens C177 from "we need this theorem" to "we need *this* theorem and here is why the neighbours fail".

Recorded as C180 with status REFUTED and its lemma extracted first, per the rule about never overwriting a failure: *when a descent produces several simultaneous conditions, test each candidate closure separately — shapes that look equally strong can differ completely in solvability.* The witnesses are now a permanent assertion in [U320_regression_checks.py](code/U320_regression_checks.py) (8 checks), so the shortcut cannot be re-proposed without the counterexamples surfacing. Harness 69/69.

CONTEXT = {
    "conjecture": "Beal: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and gcd(A,B,C)=1 has no solutions.",
    "failure_mode_1": "U113 found that U97 and U102 both refute isogeny / l-adic isomorphism / "
                      "endomorphism-algebra equality and conclude a residual mod-17 congruence is "
                      "impossible. That inference is invalid: non-isogenous abelian varieties routinely "
                      "share a residual mod-p representation (verified exactly with curves having "
                      "rational 5-torsion, a_p = p+1 mod 5 while a_p differ over Z).",
    "failure_mode_2": "U113 found that U105 uses rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8 over k = Q(sqrt5) to bound "
                      "C^-(k), while solutions give points of degree 10 over k (minimal polynomial "
                      "x^10 + 256). The bound is silent about those points.",
}


def summarize(path: Path, limit: int = 5000) -> dict:
    text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
    head = text[:limit]
    return {"filename": path.name, "excerpt": head,
            "length_chars": len(text)}


def main() -> int:
    paths = sorted(CKPT.glob("*.md"))
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        paths = [p for p in paths if any(a in p.name for a in sys.argv[1:])]
    states = [{**CONTEXT, "checkpoint": summarize(p)} for p in paths]
    print(f"screening {len(paths)} checkpoints via Jev ...", file=sys.stderr)
    responses = jev.ask_many(states, QUESTIONS)
    rows = []
    for p, st, resp in zip(paths, states, responses):
        if "error" in resp:
            print(f"  ! {p.name}: {resp['error']}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        jev.persist(f"screen_{p.stem}", st, QUESTIONS, resp)
        a = resp["answers"]
        rows.append({
            "file": p.name,
            "fm1": round(a["fm1_residual_isogeny"]["score"], 2),
            "fm2": round(a["fm2_chabauty_wrong_field"]["score"], 2),
            "overclaim": round(a["overclaimed_language"]["noul"], 2),
            "action": a["audit_priority"]["choice"],
            "conf": round(a["audit_priority"]["confidence"], 2),
        })
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(max(r["fm1"], r["fm2"]) + r["overclaim"]))
    print(json.dumps({"state": "HYPOTHESIS_ONLY", "screen": rows}, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I ran a Jev screen for the U322 failure mode across all 178 pool candidates; it independently routed to the candidate that actually carried the flaw, and surfaced two stale entries that four earlier audit passes had missed. Both corrected in place. Beal unchanged: no proof, no counterexample.

**The division of labour the project mandates**, applied properly this time: reasoning found the mode (a Prop whose hypotheses admit a degenerate instance, making it false and everything downstream vacuous), Jev found the instances. [U326_vacuity_screen.py](code/U326_vacuity_screen.py), four narrow questions per candidate, all results stored `HYPOTHESIS_ONLY`.

| action | count |
|---|---|
| no_action | 110 |
| add_control | 50 |
| restate_hypotheses | 11 |
| countersearch_now | 7 |

Of the seven `countersearch_now` hits, only **C177** clears the ~0.5 confidence threshold this project treats as signal (0.57); the rest are ≤0.22. That C177 came back first is the screen's own control — the one candidate known to have carried the mode is the one it ranked.

**Two real findings:**

1. **C015**, the pool's only PROMISING candidate, carried three obligations that are now simply false: *"no Lean toolchain is installed, so NOTHING in formal/ has ever been checked"*, *"7 sorry occurrences"*, *"5 axioms carry the entire mathematical content"*. The root chain builds with zero `sorry` and zero custom axioms, and all five axioms became named Props. Its one surviving obligation is statement fidelity.
2. **C123**'s claim text still asserts *"rank ≤ 2 … cannot carry three independent exponents"* — precisely the statement U309 refuted. Its accessory-parameter identity `2 − rig = (n−1)(n−2)` is correct and stands; only the exponent-carrying reading is withdrawn.

Both are the same layering defect this repo has been bitten by before, this time inside the pool itself. Not done: the 50 `add_control` hits were not individually audited; most are old bounded-search candidates in a category the survey gate already marks dead.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

Two things this cycle: the fidelity obligation on the pool's only PROMISING candidate is now machine-checked, and then the build environment broke underneath me — mathlib's package directory vanished and `git` is non-functional. I am re-fetching mathlib now; until it finishes I cannot re-verify anything.

**Fidelity work (verified before the breakage).** [FidelityCheck.lean](formal/Beal/FidelityCheck.lean) now holds 16 machine-checked examples. The six earlier ones covered the gcd trap, exponent 2, exponent 1, keeping base 1, and preserving the equation. Added:

- zero base rejected on `A`, `B`, `C` **separately**; zero exponent rejected on `x`, `y`, `z` separately;
- `gcd3 4 6 9 = 1` while `Nat.gcd 4 6 = 2` — triple and pairwise gcd conditions are genuinely different conjectures;
- **`2³ + 2³ = 2⁴`** — a true Beal-shape identity with all exponents ≥ 3 that fails to be a counterexample *solely* because `gcd3 2 2 2 = 2`. This is the sharpest of the set: it isolates exactly what the gcd condition does;
- `BealConjecture` instantiated at exponent 1000, which no bounded version yields;
- `A^x < C^z` and `B^y < C^z`, so the three powers cannot be permuted.

That closes C015's surviving obligation for `IsBealCounterexample` and `BealConjecture`. What remains, recorded on C182: fidelity of the fourteen named Props against their cited sources, which needs primary sources not all held in `references/`.

**The environment problem, stated plainly.** After that build succeeded, the next `lake build` failed: `.lake/packages/mathlib` is gone, and `/usr/bin/git` is broken because `xcode-select -p` points at a damaged Xcode install (`dyld: Library not loaded: DVTSystemPrerequisites.framework`). I did not delete anything — my commands inside that directory were `ls`, `grep`, `sed -n`. Disk has 58 GB free, so it is not space.

Workaround in progress: `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git` works (2.50.1), so I put it on `PATH` and lake is re-fetching — 710 MB down so far, running in the background. A permanent fix needs `sudo xcode-select --switch /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`, which is yours to run, not mine.

Everything reported through the 16 fidelity examples was genuinely checked. Nothing after that is verified until the fetch completes and I rebuild.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I acted on the Jev screen instead of just recording it: the three highest-ranked "empty search, no control" candidates now have planted-instance controls, and all three pass. Lean is still rebuilding after the environment breakage. No proof, no counterexample.

**Why these three needed it.** C156 (conf 0.95), C081 (0.78), C045 (0.72) each rested on a bounded search that found nothing, with nothing showing the searcher *could* find something. That is the exact shape of this project's two recorded false positives — U164 (PARI `sqrt` returning a float, so `issquare` tested a `t_REAL`) and U166 (misreading one surviving residue class as "only n = 0").

[U328_search_controls.py](code/U328_search_controls.py), now in the harness:

- **C156** — shift the curve constant by 256 so `y = 2` gives `512 = 8³`; the searcher must return `(2,8)`. It does.
- **C045** — `is_perfect_power_ge2` checked on `8 = 2³`, `9 = 3²`, and `7` (not a power); Gaussian arithmetic checked against `(1+2i)³ = −11−2i` and `(2+i)² = 3+4i`.
- **C081** — the congruence stage is fed three base pairs with *genuine* solutions (`3³+6³ = 3⁵`, `2³+2³ = 2⁴`, `7⁶+7⁷ = 98³`) and must not kill any. It doesn't.

A passing control rules out a broken searcher and nothing more — none of the three becomes evidence for Beal, and bounded search stays a dead category. I did **not** control the other 47 `add_control` hits: most are older bounded-search candidates in that same dead category, so the cost isn't justified. That judgement is recorded on C183 rather than silently acted on.

**Also fixed:** the `MEMORY.md` index line still advertised *"why no rigid object carries three Beal exponents"* — the headline U309 refuted. Corrected; that was the fourth layer of the same propagation.

**Environment status:** mathlib re-fetched (404 MB of oleans rebuilt so far) using `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git`, since `/usr/bin/git` is broken by a damaged Xcode install. Full `lake build` is still running in the background. Nothing Lean-side is re-verified until it completes; a permanent fix needs `sudo xcode-select --switch /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`, which is yours to run.

        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r["value"] + r["compat"] - r["shared_fail"]))

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I executed the RESTART that C184 called for — into effective Diophantine geometry, the one survey direction this session hadn't touched — and priced it before entering: the genus is unbounded over the Beal range, so it fails on a **different** wall from automorphy. Lean still rebuilding (1320/2662). No proof, no counterexample.

**The computation.** For a fixed hyperbolic signature the Darmon–Granville curve is a Galois cover of P¹ branched over `{0,1,∞}` with ramification `(x,y,z)`, so Riemann–Hurwitz gives `g = 1 + N|χ|/2`. With `N = lcm(x,y,z)` as a lower-bound degree proxy:

| signature | lcm | \|χ\| | genus ≥ |
|---|---|---|---|
| (3,4,5) | 60 | 13/60 | 15/2 |
| (3,5,7) | 105 | 34/105 | 18 |
| (13,17,19) | 4199 | 3408/4199 | 1705 |
| (3,4,9973) | — | — | 49855/2 |

**My own control caught an error.** I first asserted the minimum `|χ|` over Beal signatures was 1/12 — it failed, because **(3,3,3) gives `|χ| = 0`**: euclidean, not hyperbolic. That's FLT3, and the hyperbolicity condition is a real restriction inside the Beal range rather than automatic. Fixed, and the failure is preserved in the script's comments. The corrected floor is 1/12 at (3,3,4), against 1/42 at (2,3,7) for Fermat–Catalan — so the geometrically hardest cases are exactly the exponent-2 ones Beal excludes.

**Why this was worth doing even though it's blocked.** Faltings gives finiteness per signature but ineffectively; effectivity is open for a single genus-≥2 curve in general, and Beal needs it for infinitely many curves of growing genus plus control of the twists. Automorphy (C171/C174) fails on the **rank of one object**; this fails on **uniformity over a growing family**. Two distinct walls recorded beats mining either — which is the diversity-of-failure-mechanism the loop asks for.

Recorded as C185 with its gaps named: the degree proxy is a lower bound (safe for the unboundedness conclusion), and the twist count, where class-group input enters, is not computed at all.

Two hard-won facts from the Sept 2026 Beal sessions:

1. **Both-summands-are-powers trick.** In A^x+B^y=C^z both summands are perfect powers, so on a
   classical parametrisation (ℤ[i] for (2m,2n,z odd), Euclid for all-even) the "good" branch (the
   parameter not divisible by the bad prime) is available on at least one side. Combined with a
   ONE-SIDED published theorem (Bennett–Skinner Thm 1.1, C=3) it closed (2m,2n,3) for all m,n ≥ 2
   (with a rank-0 curve y²=x³+27 for the exponent-3 side). It does NOT extend to z=5 (Bennett's
   diagonal proof pairs the sides) or z ≥ 7 (no one-sided identity over ℚ, C049).

2. **Fermat–Catalan blindness test (C053).** 14 of 15 elementary kernel conditions hold on the ten
   exponent-2 Fermat–Catalan solutions, so they carry no Beal-specific content. Every new elementary
   condition must be run through `code/U141_countersearch_fc.py` first.

**Why:** two cycles were lost re-deriving literature ("parametrise then cite" reproduces BCDY rows),
and the pool converged twice on residue sieves that provably cannot separate exponent 2 from ≥3.

**How to apply:** before any elementary cycle, run the blindness test; before any parametrisation
cycle, check BCDY 2015 Tables 1–3 and the 2024 survey (saved in `references/U130/`). Related:
[[jev-use-aggressively]], [[beal-exploration-loop]].

**Added 2026-09-18 (U167–U177), two more durable lessons:**
3. **Instance check before calling a signature open.** (4,4,p) is an instance of x²+y⁴=zⁿ (Bennett–Ellenberg–Ng 2010), closed for all n ≥ 4; I had listed it open from an older abstract. Run `code/U168_instance_closure.py` (rows + odd-exponent sign moves) on any "open" signature first.
4. **Even hyperelliptic curves have elliptic quotients.** A genus-2 curve y² = f(x²) maps to y² = f(X) and y² = X³f(1/X); check their ranks in PARI before declaring "needs Chabauty".

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I discharged C187's literature obligation by checking all eleven solved-signature rows against the primary sources actually held in `references/U130/` — every one is located. My first matcher produced a false "unlocated" and I fixed the matcher, not the row. Lean at 1548/2662. No proof, no counterexample.

**Why this layer matters.** The rows in [U168_instance_closure.py](code/U168_instance_closure.py) decide which signatures the repo calls CLOSED. A wrong row silently marks an open case done — the exact shape of the defect that produced the second audit notice. The sources are held, so this is a primary-source literature check doable at $0.

All eleven located: Wiles, `(3,4,5)`, `(3,4,4)` in the 2024 survey; `(n,n,2)`, `(n,n,3)` in Darmon–Merel; `(2,4,n)` in BEN 2010; `(3,3,2n)`, `(3,6,n)`, `(4,2n,3)` in BCDY 2015; the three Dahmen–Siksek rows; `(2,3,7)` in PSS.

**The false negative is the instructive part.** BEN 2010 writes the signature as `A⁴ + B² = Cᵖ` — square **second** — and my regex looked for `x² + y⁴`. That was my matcher being too literal. I fixed it and kept the episode in the script's comments, because *"unlocated" must mean "not in the source", never "my regex missed"*. Had I recorded the first run's verdict, I'd have manufactured a fake defect.

**Control**, so the matcher isn't trivially permissive: it asserts the survey does **not** claim `(3,5,7)` is solved. If it did, the repo's "open" label would be wrong. The assertion holds.

**What string matching cannot do**, recorded as C188's obligation: whether each theorem's *exact hypotheses* match how the row is used — coprimality conventions, exclusion of zero and unit bases, and whether a row stated over ℤ is being applied over ℕ. That needs a human reading the PDFs, and I have not done it.

Reading the held source instead of the repo's summary of it surfaced an unstated dependency in the closure layer: Darmon–Merel close only *non-trivial* solutions, so their rows never covered a **base of 1** — the exact trap the target discipline names. No verdict changes; the case is covered elsewhere, by Mihailescu. Lean at 1617/2662. No proof, no counterexample.

**What the source actually says**, verbatim in `references/U130/darmon_merel.txt`: *"a solution is called trivial if xyz = 0 or ±1"*. So every row taken from Darmon–Merel — 25 of the 74 closures, the largest single contributor — carries a hypothesis the instance-closure tool did not record.

**Why it isn't a mathematical error.** A Beal case with a base of 1 is `1 + B^y = C^z` with `y,z ≥ 3` — Catalan's equation, closed by Mihailescu. The repo already carries that in [Mihailescu.lean](formal/Beal/Mihailescu.lean): `beal_base_a_ne_one`, `beal_base_b_ne_one`, `beal_counterexample_bases_ge_two`, each taking the named `MihailescuTheorem`. What was missing was the *record* that every "closed" verdict means **closed for bases ≥ 2 by the cited row, and for a base of 1 by Mihailescu**. Neither half may be dropped.

Fixed in place: [U168_instance_closure.py](code/U168_instance_closure.py) now carries the dependency in its header, and the regression guard (now 9 checks) asserts three things — that the triviality convention is really in the held source, that the tool still records the dependency, and that the three Mihailescu theorems still exist.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

I verified the `(2,3,7)` closure row against Poonen–Schaefer–Stoll's Theorem 1.1 itself — all 16 primitive solutions confirmed exactly, none usable as a Beal instance — and found that the row depends on a positivity condition the repo had not written down. Lean at 1679/2662. No proof, no counterexample.

**The check.** A Beal instance with `2∣x, 3∣y, 7∣z` gives `X = A^{x/2}` with `x ≥ 4` even, so `X` must be a perfect power of exponent ≥ 2, with `Y, Z > 0`. Against the 16 listed triples:

- **14 are killed by positivity** — they contain a `0` or a negative entry, which Beal excludes: `(1,−1,0)`, `(3,−2,1)`, `(71,−17,2)`, `(21063928,−76271,17)`, and the sign variants.
- **2 survive positivity** — `(2213459, 1414, 65)` and `(15312283, 9262, 113)`, both genuine positive solutions of `x²+y³=z⁷` — and are killed because neither `x` is a perfect power.

**The fragile part.** `x = ±1` *is* a perfect power (`1 = 1²`), so the perfect-power test does **not** exclude those triples; only positivity does. If the row were ever restated without the positivity condition it would become **false**. That is C189's base-1 rider appearing a second time, in a different row, and it is now asserted in the regression guard (10 checks) along with a non-vacuity control on the detector — it must hit on `1` and `64` and miss on `2213459`.

This is the second of five outstanding hypothesis-level source reads, and I picked it because it is the row where an exponent 2 appears, which is the trap-rich zone. The row survives, but for reasons that were not recorded. **Still not done:** BEN 2010, Bennett–Skinner, BCDY, Dahmen–Siksek.

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

Two more source reads, with two findings: the row sources use **different triviality conventions**, so the base-1 rider is needed for some rows and not others — and no GRH-conditional signature is being used as unconditional. Lean at 1720/2662. No proof, no counterexample.

**Finding (a): the conventions differ.**

| source | triviality convention | needs the C189 base-1 rider? |
|---|---|---|
| Darmon–Merel | *"trivial if xyz = 0 **or ±1**"* | **yes** |
| Dahmen–Siksek | *"non-trivial if xyz ≠ 0"* | **no** |

Dahmen–Siksek's Theorems 1 and 2 list the *complete* coprime solution sets — `(±1,∓1,0)`, `(±1,0,±1)`, `(0,±1,±1)` — every one of which has a zero entry. So no positive solution exists at all, and a base of 1 is already covered. Treating the two sources uniformly is precisely what hid the C189 gap. Finding that one row needs a rider and another does not is more useful than finding that both do.

**Finding (b): GRH discipline holds.** Dahmen–Siksek prove `(5,5,11)`, `(5,5,13)` and `(7,7,11)` **only under GRH**. None of the three appears in the closure tool. That matters because "heuristic laundering" — relabelling a GRH-conditional result as unconditional — is one of the three recurring failure modes this repo records, and here it was avoided.

Both facts are now asserted in the regression guard (11 checks), so a future edit that either drops a convention or promotes a GRH row will fail rather than pass silently.

Three of five sources read. **Still not done:** BEN 2010, Bennett–Skinner, BCDY.

def divisors(n): return [d for d in range(2,n+1) if n%d==0]
def instance(sig):
    ours=[(sig[0],+1),(sig[1],+1),(sig[2],-1)]
    for perm in itertools.permutations(range(3)):
        for da in divisors(ours[perm[0]][0]):
          for db in divisors(ours[perm[1]][0]):
            for dc in divisors(ours[perm[2]][0]):
                row=(da,db,dc); slots=(+1,+1,-1)
                for name,f in NOSOL.items():
                    if not f(*row): continue
                    for g in (+1,-1):
                        ok=all(ours[perm[i]][1]*g==slots[i] or row[i]%2==1 for i in range(3))
                        if ok: return name,row,perm
    return None
P=[3,4,5,7,11,13,17,19]
open_,closed=[],{}
for sig in itertools.product(P,repeat=3):
    if sig[0]>sig[1]: continue            # A,B symmetric
    r=instance(sig)
    if r: closed[sig]=r[0]
    else: open_.append(sig)
print("reduced signatures tested:",len(closed)+len(open_)," closed by instance:",len(closed)," open:",len(open_))
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(closed.values()).most_common())
print("OPEN containing a 4:",[s for s in open_ if 4 in s][:40])
print("OPEN all odd, smallest:",[s for s in open_ if 4 not in s][:25])
json.dump({"closed":{str(k):v for k,v in closed.items()},"open":open_},open("research/pool/evidence/instance_closure_U168.json","w"))

That matters for how `BennettSkinnerThree` is stated in [EvenEvenThree.lean](formal/Beal/EvenEvenThree.lean): it fixes `C = 3`, and 3 is not among the exceptional pairs, so the exceptions do not bite.

**The headline from the whole audit:** the five sources use **three distinct triviality conventions** — exclude `{0, ±1}`, exclude `{0}` only, exclude nothing beyond coprimality. That is why the rows cannot be summarised uniformly, and it is exactly where the base-1 gap hid.

## 🤖 Assistant  ·  `[TIMESTAMP]`

# We have not solved Beal's conjecture yet.

Checking the build's extent by computation rather than trusting the prose found that **four** Lean files are outside the build, not one as VERIFIED.md claimed. Lean at 1956/2662. No proof, no counterexample.

**The correction.** `lakefile.lean` sets `roots := #[\`Beal]`, so `lake build` covers only the transitive import closure of `Beal.lean` — **29 of 33 files**. Outside it entirely:

`SquarefreeCore.lean` · `Valuation.lean` · `FermatCatalan.lean` · `GaussianObstruction.lean`

Nothing in those is type-checked by any build, so nothing in them may be cited. VERIFIED.md named only the first, which overstated the coverage — the same pattern as the README superlative in C187: not wrong about what it said, incomplete about everything else.

**What prompted the check** was noticing `Structure.lean` is not in `Beal.lean`'s direct import list. It *is* reachable transitively (via `Residual`, `EvenEvenThree`, `Necessary`, `SameOddPrime`, `MordellFixedBase`), so the theorems I added to it this session — `support_disjoint_*`, `tame_valuation_at_*` — really are inside the build. But that was luck, not design, and I only know it because I computed the closure.

**The axiom claim now has a checked reason.** All four custom axiom declarations in the repository live in `SquarefreeCore.lean`, and the new guard (13 checks) asserts that *every* file containing a custom `axiom` is outside the build. So "zero custom axioms in the root chain" holds because it is enforced, not because it was once observed.

**Not done:** the three newly-identified excluded files have never been checked and their contents are unknown. They should either be imported and fixed or deleted; I have done neither, and C195 records that.
